title: Cisco CCNA 200-301 Study Guide
description: The Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) is the foundational networking certification from Cisco, earned by passing a single exam: 200-301. It runs 120 minutes, costs $400 USD, is offered in English only, and is graded pass/fail with results online within 48 hours. The blueprint covers network fundamentals, network access, IP connectivity, IP services, security fundamentals, and automation and programmability — and the simulation questions put you at a command line, so configuration has to be muscle memory rather than recognition.
audience: Help desk and support technicians moving toward infrastructure, career changers targeting networking or network security, and developers and cloud engineers who keep hitting routing and subnetting they do not understand. There are no prerequisites. Cisco suggests around a year of hands-on experience with its solutions, but a large share of candidates pass on lab time alone — Packet Tracer, GNS3 or a shelf of second-hand switches all count.
why_get_it: CCNA establishes credibility in networking. It demonstrates you understand how IP networks function—not just that you followed a tutorial. Employers use it as a baseline filter for network technician and junior engineer roles. The exam covers real-world skills: subnetting, routing protocols, switching, VLANs, security fundamentals, and network automation basics. It also satisfies a meaningful portion of the knowledge base needed for higher-level Cisco and non-Cisco certifications.
when_to_get_it: Take CCNA if you want to work in networking, network security or infrastructure, and take it early: it opens doors before you have the experience to open them yourself, and it is named in job postings more often than any other networking credential. Budget two to four months. If you want something cheaper, broader and vendor-neutral first, Network+ covers similar ground at a fraction of the price — but if networking is the destination rather than a stepping stone, most people are better off going straight to CCNA. With two or more years of hands-on networking behind you and a senior role in view, consider going directly to CCNP. Note the version timing: the current v1.1 exam has a last test date of 2 February 2027, and the refreshed v2.0 blueprint launches the next day under the same 200-301 code.
salary_note: Entry-level roles—network technician, junior network engineer, and help-desk-to-networking transitions—typically start around $55K–$70K. With 2–3 years of hands-on experience, network engineer roles commonly reach $85K–$110K. Specializing in network automation or advancing to CCNP pushes compensation past $120K. Figures vary widely by region, employer, and the full scope of your skills.
exam_format: Multiple choice, drag-and-drop, and simulation questions. Approximately 100–120 questions. Version note: the current v1.1 exam has a last test date of Feb 2, 2027 — the refreshed 'new CCNA' v2.0 (adds AI topics, restructures to 5 domains) launches Feb 3, 2027 under the SAME 200-301 code. Testing in 2026? Study v1.1 materials confidently. Planning for mid-2027 or later? Wait for v2.0-aligned materials.
exam_questions: 100–120 questions (approximate; Cisco does not publish the exact count)
recertification_note: CCNA is valid for 3 years. Renew by passing any Cisco exam, completing continuing education credits through the Cisco Continuing Education Program, or earning a higher-level Cisco certification.

study_steps.title: Understand the exam scope
study_steps.description: Download the official CCNA 200-301 exam topics from Cisco's website. Review every topic area before buying any course material. Knowing what the exam actually covers prevents wasted study time on irrelevant material.

study_steps.title: Learn networking fundamentals first
study_steps.description: If you are new to networking, start with the OSI model, IP addressing, and subnetting before touching a video course. Subnetting must become second nature before exam day. Use practice tools until you can subnet quickly without a calculator.

study_steps.title: Work through a primary video course
study_steps.description: Choose one comprehensive video course and work through it completely. Do not jump between multiple courses at the same time. Udemy instructors like Jeremy's IT Lab offer full CCNA courses that align directly with the exam topics. Watch, pause, and practice as you go.

study_steps.title: Read supporting material
study_steps.description: The official Cisco Press CCNA 200-301 Official Cert Guide (two-volume set) is the most thorough written resource. Use it alongside your video course to reinforce concepts, especially for topics that need more depth than video alone provides.

study_steps.title: Build hands-on lab skills
study_steps.description: Cisco Packet Tracer (free, requires a Cisco Networking Academy account) is the primary lab tool for most CCNA candidates. GNS3 and EVE-NG are alternatives for those who want closer-to-real-hardware simulation. Lab work is not optional—the exam includes simulation questions.

study_steps.title: Take practice exams
study_steps.description: Begin practice exams once you have covered all topics. Boson ExSim is widely considered the gold standard for CCNA practice tests. Aim to consistently score above 85% before scheduling your real exam. Review every wrong answer—understand why, not just what.

study_steps.title: Review weak areas systematically
study_steps.description: Use your practice exam results to identify weak areas. Return to your video course, notes, or the official cert guide for those specific topics. Repeat targeted practice until the weak areas become strengths.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Schedule your exam through Pearson VUE. You can take it at a testing center or online proctored. Book about two weeks out to give yourself a clear deadline. The exam is 120 minutes. Arrive rested and do not cram the night before.

faq.question: Is CCNA good for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, if you are serious about networking. It is not a trivial certification—expect 3 to 6 months of dedicated study. But it is designed as an entry-level credential and does not require prior IT experience to pass.

faq.question: How long does it take to study for CCNA?
faq.answer: Most candidates spend 3 to 6 months studying part-time. Those with existing networking experience may prepare in 6 to 8 weeks. Those brand new to IT should plan for the longer end of that range.

faq.question: How hard is the CCNA exam?
faq.answer: It is a legitimately challenging exam. The simulation questions require hands-on skill, not just memorization. Consistent study over several months, combined with lab practice and practice exams, is what separates passing candidates from failing ones.

faq.question: What score do you need to pass CCNA?
faq.answer: Cisco uses a scaled scoring system with a maximum score of 1000. The passing score for CCNA 200-301 is 825. Cisco does not publish individual question weights.

faq.question: Can I get a job with just CCNA?
faq.answer: Yes. CCNA is recognized by employers as a qualification for network technician, junior network engineer, and helpdesk-to-networking transition roles. Pairing it with hands-on homelab or real work experience significantly improves job prospects.

faq.question: Is CompTIA Network+ better than CCNA?
faq.answer: They serve different goals. Network+ is vendor-neutral and broader; CCNA is vendor-specific and deeper. CCNA carries more weight in enterprise networking roles. Network+ is a reasonable first step if you want a gentler introduction before committing to CCNA.

faq.question: What certification comes after CCNA?
faq.answer: The natural progression is CCNP Enterprise for networking roles, CCNP Security for security roles, or CCNA Automation (formerly Cisco DevNet Associate) for automation/programmability. The path depends on the direction you want to take your career.

faq.question: Does CCNA expire?
faq.answer: Yes. CCNA is valid for three years. Renew it by passing any Cisco exam, completing Cisco Continuing Education credits, or earning a higher-level Cisco certification before the expiration date.
